label: adjudicate-risk-review-2
tail:
Done. All gates green.

## What the dispatch actually found

**The three detectors it named printed zero candidates** — `boundary-audit`, `citation-fidelity` and `gate-liveness` all exited 0 on first run. The read-group join failed on the contingency command, `risk-report --require-reviewed`, with exactly one open item. That was the whole job.

Two contingency branches in the brief **did not apply**, and I didn't manufacture work to fill them:
- **finite-smoke was not vacuous** — 4 live checks, selected by lane `contract-audit-3`. The branch telling me to add Sylow/unit-group/poset checks is premised on `0 checks`. Adding more to an already-live gate is the toy-check failure the same paragraph forbids.
- **No candidate rows existed** to fix or uphold. The 2 `UPHELD BY REVIEW` lines are `contract-audit-1`'s prior work being reported back.

## The one finding

`thm-extension-generated-by-separable-elements-is-separable`, CRITICAL 14, batch 3 — and the reason it lacked a review turned out to matter. This is the case QUALITY-CONTROLS documents: **a repair newly routed it here.** Both judge lanes independently rejected the *previous* text for the same defect (a circular appeal to transitivity — the tower steps were never shown elementwise separable). That was adjudicated `confirmed_fatal` by both and repaired at step 8 on the separable-degree route, ledger row `frontier-15-S8-03`. The rewrite's six added dependencies are what pushed the score to critical, leaving a critical item unreviewed.

**Disposition: no defect.** What I checked:

- **Step 2.1, the load-bearing step, is exactly licensed** — not conveniently, but by definition. `def-repeated-root-and-separable-polynomial` defines separable as "no repeated root in *any* extension field of $F$", and every extension of $E_{j-1}$ is one of $F$, so the divisor inherits it.
- **The circularity probe** — the axis that actually earned the tier, since circularity was the judged defect. The full transitive cone is **413 items, acyclic, and never reaches this theorem**; the primitive element theorem, reached via `[L8]`, doesn't depend on it either.
- **The repair closes the defect rather than relocating it** — the new proof never claims an intermediate layer is elementwise separable; it needs only per-step degree equality, so the judges' objection has no target in the current text.
- Three of the score's signals are lexical artifacts of *cited* text: the biconditional points come from `[L8]`'s "if and only if" (used in one direction only, so the `iff` rows conceal no reversed implication), and the quotient points from `[L4]`'s quoted $F[x]/(m_a)$ — no quotient is constructed anywhere.

**Independent refuter:** DeepSeek V4 Pro, single item packed at 31KB — comfortably inside the budget that defeated the prior lane at 3+ items, which is why this one completed where 40 of its 92 didn't. Zero fatal, zero nonfatal, and it independently flagged the same two 30-second closures in 1.1 and 1.2 that I did.

## Two things worth your attention

**I edited no item text.** The two compressed inferences are genuine 30-second closures, and step 8 withdraws the polish licence — an edit there voids the verdict and forces a rejudge for a gap a reader closes in a sentence. Recorded in the notes instead.

**The repaired item still needs its rejudge.** Its hash moved off the rejected text, so the current pair verdict is stale by construction. That's the engine's `8-rejudge` stage, not mine, and `level-coverage --verify-current-context` will hold until it runs.

I also left the 518 generated boundary rows open as `contract-audit-1` recorded them (`f15-a-rr-005`) — this item's own `endpoints` row is one of that family, template-spliced prose ("For An algebraic extension…") though its content is true. It wasn't a printed candidate, so it was outside this dispatch; named in the report rather than silently passed.

Files changed: one `risk_review` (+7/−1, verified as exactly 1 of 59 entries), the re-merge, the refuter record, and the report section. No new defect-ledger row — I found no new defect, and writing one would have been false.
